subject: hindi
book: Aroh Bhag 2 (आरोह भाग 2); Vitan Bhag 2 (वितान भाग 2)

chapters.title: आरोह: हरिवंश राय बच्चन — आत्म-परिचय; एक गीत (दिन जल्दी-जल्दी ढलता है)

concepts.text: Harivansh Rai Bachchan (1907-2003), born in Allahabad; poet of हालावाद and post-Chhayavad lyric poetry
Works: मधुशाला, मधुबाला, मधुकलश, निशा निमंत्रण, एकांत संगीत, मिलन यामिनी, दो चट्टानें (Sahitya Akademi)
Four-part autobiography: क्या भूलूँ क्या याद करूँ, नीड़ का निर्माण फिर, बसेरे से दूर, दशद्वार से सोपान तक
The poet carries the burden of worldly life yet keeps love in his heart
He drinks the wine of affection and cares little for the world's opinion
The world praises those who sing its tune; the poet sings what his heart feels
He and the world are different; he feels no tie with it ('मैं और, और जग और')
He carries youthful passion (उन्माद) and sorrow (अवसाद) together
Paradoxes: tears that hold melody, cool words that hold fire
He wears the dress of a madman (दीवाना) and carries the message of joy and intoxication
Self-knowledge: knowing oneself means knowing both the world and its contradictions

sections.name: 1.3 कविता 2: एक गीत (दिन जल्दी-जल्दी ढलता है)

concepts.text: From निशा निमंत्रण; the day ends quickly, reminding us how time slips by
A traveller hurries, fearing night will fall before he reaches his destination
Mother birds fly faster thinking of their young waiting in the nest
The poet asks: who is waiting eagerly for me? (loneliness after losing his wife)
That question slows his steps and fills his heart with restlessness
Self and the world: love versus worldly life
Individual freedom and personal feeling in poetry
Passage of time, longing and loneliness
विरोधाभास (paradox): रोदन में राग, शीतल वाणी में आग
अनुप्रास, पुनरुक्ति प्रकाश (जल्दी-जल्दी), प्रश्न-शैली
Lyrical, singable (गीतात्मक) form; simple Khari Boli with Urdu touches
Imagery of nests, travellers and the setting sun
जग-जीवन: worldly life; स्नेह-सुरा: wine of love; उन्माद: passion; अवसाद: sadness
उद्गार: outpouring of feelings; विकल: restless; नीड़: nest
हालावाद: Bachchan's poetry of wine symbolising joy of life

sections.name: 1.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Explain the contradictions in the poet's personality
Why the poet says he and the world are different

Compare the mood of the two poems
Alok Dhanva (b. 1948), born in Munger (Bihar); poet of the 1970s
Collection: दुनिया रोज़ बनती है; well-known poems गोली दागो पोस्टर, जनता का आदमी, भागी हुई लड़कियाँ, ब्रूनो की बेटियाँ
The rainy month of Bhado ends and autumn (शरद) arrives like a bright morning
Autumn is pictured as a child on a red bicycle, ringing its bell and calling other children
The sky becomes soft and clear so kites can fly
Kites are the lightest, most colourful thing, made of thin paper and bamboo
Children seem born with cotton: soft and light
The earth runs to meet their restless feet as they race on rooftops
They play the directions like a drum (मृदंग) with their running
They run on dangerous roof edges, but the rhythm of their bodies keeps them safe
Kites carry their dreams high; when they fall and survive, they grow more fearless
Joy, energy and freedom of childhood
Change of season and the beauty of nature
Children's fearlessness and growing up
मानवीकरण: autumn as a child on a bicycle
बिंब (imagery): visual, sound and motion images
उपमा, उत्प्रेक्षा; free verse with lively rhythm
भादो: rainy month; शरद: autumn; पतंग: kite
कपास: cotton; मृदंग: drum; मुंडेर: roof edge
रोमांचित, पेंग: swing, thrill

sections.name: 2.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: How the poet describes the arrival of autumn

chapters.title: आरोह: कुँवर नारायण — कविता के बहाने; बात सीधी थी पर

concepts.text: Kunwar Narayan (1927-2017), Faizabad/Lucknow; poet of तीसरा सप्तक
Works: चक्रव्यूह, परिवेश: हम-तुम, आत्मजयी, अपने सामने, कोई दूसरा नहीं, इन दिनों
Jnanpith Award (2005)
Poetry is like a bird's flight, but a bird cannot know the reach of poetry
Poetry is like a flower blooming, but a flower withers while poetry lasts
Poetry is like children's play: it breaks boundaries between homes and people
Poetry has limitless possibilities beyond time and place
A simple idea got tangled because the poet wanted fancy language
He kept twisting words like a screw that loses its threads (चूड़ी मर जाना)
He hammered it in like a nail; onlookers praised the show (वाह-वाह)
The idea, like a naughty child, mocked his effort
Lesson: use language simply and naturally; matter matters more than ornament
Nature and reach of poetry
Relation between content (कथ्य) and form (भाषा)
Simplicity of expression
मानवीकरण (बात as a naughty child), उपमा, दृष्टांत
Images of birds, flowers, children, screws and nails
Idioms: पेंच कसना, चूड़ी मरना, ज़ोर-ज़बरदस्ती
बहाना: pretext; उड़ान: flight; सहूलियत: ease
पेंच, कील, चूड़ी: screw, nail, thread
तमाशबीन: onlookers; करतब: feat

chapters.title: आरोह: रघुवीर सहाय — कैमरे में बंद अपाहिज

concepts.text: Raghuvir Sahay (1929-1990), Lucknow; poet of दूसरा सप्तक and journalist (editor of दिनमान)
Works: सीढ़ियों पर धूप में, आत्महत्या के विरुद्ध, हँसो हँसो जल्दी हँसो, लोग भूल गए हैं (Sahitya Akademi)
A TV programme brings a disabled man to the studio to show his pain
The anchor asks insensitive questions: are you disabled, why are you disabled
He keeps asking how it feels, to make the man cry on camera
The camera zooms in on his eyes for a close-up of his pain
The anchor wants viewers to cry too, for the programme's success
Time on screen is costly; when the man doesn't cry, the anchor says the programme fell just short
The media calls itself strong and capable while using the weak
Satire on media insensitivity and commercialisation
Pain sold as a product (TRP culture)
Disability and dignity
Dramatic (नाटकीय) form; dialogue
Brackets used as stage/camera directions
Sharp irony and satire
अपाहिज: disabled; दूरदर्शन, कैमरा, परदा: media words
समर्थ, शक्तिवान: powerful; दुर्बल: weak
कसर: shortfall

concepts.text: Why the poem is a satire on media

Shamsher Bahadur Singh (1911-1993), born in Dehradun; poet of दूसरा सप्तक; also a painter
Works: कुछ कविताएँ, कुछ और कविताएँ, चुका भी हूँ नहीं मैं (Sahitya Akademi), इतने पास अपने, बात बोलेगी
The dawn sky is like a blue conch (नीला शंख)
Like a hearth (चौका) freshly plastered with ash, still damp
Like a black grinding stone (सिल) washed with a little red saffron
Like a slate rubbed with red chalk
Like a fair, shimmering body moving in blue water
The magic of dawn ends as the sun rises
Changing colours of the dawn sky
Village life images used for nature
Experimental new imagery
उपमा, उत्प्रेक्षा; visual images (चित्रात्मकता)
Painterly use of colour; free verse
Village household images: चौका, सिल, स्लेट
उषा: dawn; शंख: conch; चौका: kitchen hearth
सिल: grinding stone; केसर: saffron; खड़िया: chalk
जादू टूटना: magic ending

sections.name: 5.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Identify images and say what each shows about dawn
Why the poem is called a 'word-picture'
सप्रसंग व्याख्या; identify devices
Nirala (1899-1961), born at Mahishadal, Midnapore (West Bengal); a pillar of Chhayavad
Works: अनामिका, परिमल, गीतिका, कुकुरमुत्ता, नए पत्ते, राम की शक्तिपूजा, सरोज स्मृति
Pioneer of free verse (मुक्त छंद) in Hindi
Unstable joy floats on the sea of wind with the shadow of sorrow
The cloud is called the hero of revolution (विप्लव के वीर)
Thunder wakes sprouts hidden in the earth
Small plants wave their hands and call the cloud
The rich tremble in their mansions; mansions are houses of fear
Tall trees are struck, but small plants survive and smile
The weak, thin farmer calls the cloud for revolution
Cloud as a symbol of revolution
Exploitation of farmers and the poor by the rich
Change and hope for the oppressed
रूपक, मानवीकरण, अनुप्रास
Symbols: cloud = revolution; small plants = the poor; mansions = the rich
Tatsam vocabulary; free verse
विप्लव: revolution; समीर: wind; अट्टालिका: mansion
कृषक: farmer; जीर्ण, शीर्ण: worn, thin
अंकुर: sprout; वज्र: thunderbolt

chapters.title: आरोह: तुलसीदास — कवितावली (उत्तर कांड से); लक्ष्मण-मूर्छा और राम का विलाप

concepts.text: Tulsidas (1532-1623), born at Rajapur, Banda (UP); poet of सगुण राम भक्ति
Works: रामचरितमानस, कवितावली, गीतावली, दोहावली, विनयपत्रिका, कृष्णगीतावली
Wrote in both Awadhi and Braj
All kinds of people (workers, farmers, traders, beggars) do every deed for their stomach
Hunger makes people sell even their children
The fire of hunger is greater than the ocean's fire; only Ram can quench it
In Kaliyug, farmers have no farming, beggars get no alms, traders no trade
Poverty is like Ravana pressing the world; prayer to Ram for help
Tulsi does not care what people call him: he lives by begging and sleeps in a mosque

sections.name: 7.3 लक्ष्मण-मूर्छा और राम का विलाप (रामचरितमानस, लंका कांड)

concepts.text: Lakshman falls unconscious in battle; Hanuman goes for the life-saving herb
Bharat shoots Hanuman by mistake; later Hanuman praises Bharat
Ram weeps like an ordinary man over Lakshman
Ram regrets: had he known he'd lose his brother, he'd not have obeyed father's order
Wife, wealth and home come again in life, but not a brother like Lakshman
Ram compares himself to a bird without wings, a snake without its gem
Ram fears facing Ayodhya: lost a brother for a wife
Hanuman arrives like heroism in the middle of sorrow
Poverty and hunger in society
Brotherly love and Ram's human grief
Faith in Ram as the only saviour
Chhand: कवित्त, सवैया (Kavitavali); दोहा, चौपाई, सोरठा (Manas)
Rasa: करुण रस in the lament, वीर रस with Hanuman
Devices: उपमा, उत्प्रेक्षा, दृष्टांत, रूपक, अनुप्रास
Language: Braj (Kavitavali), Awadhi (Manas)
किसबी: workers; बनिक: traders; भाट: bards
बड़वागि: fire in the sea; दारिद: poverty; दसानन: Ravana
मूर्छा: fainting; बिलाप: lament; संजीवनी: life-saving herb

sections.name: 7.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Explain the economic picture in the kavitts

Firaq Gorakhpuri (Raghupati Sahay, 1896-1982), born in Gorakhpur; Urdu poet
Works: गुले नग़्मा (Jnanpith), बज़्मे ज़िंदगी रंगे शायरी, रूहे-कायनात
Mother holds her moon-like child in the courtyard and rocks it
Child's laughter fills the house
Mother bathes the child in clean water, combs its hair and dresses it
Diwali evening: house cleaned, mother lights a lamp near sugar toys
Child insists on the moon; mother shows it in a mirror
Raksha Bandhan: sister ties shiny rakhi to her brother
Buds open their petals gently: arrival of beauty
Stars blink, every particle sleeps: night imagery
Both the poet and his fate cry for each other
In love you get as much as you lose yourself
His ghazals carry the voice of Mir
Rubai: four lines; first, second and fourth lines rhyme
Ghazal: sher, matla, maqta, radif, kafiya
Mother-child love (वात्सल्य)
Love, separation and fate
Hindi-Urdu-folk mixed language
Images of home and festivals
वात्सल्य रस; उपमा, रूपक
लोका देना: to rock; ठुनकना: to sulk
रस की पुतली: lovely girl; लच्छे: shiny threads
किस्मत, फ़ितरत, तवाज़ुन: fate, nature, balance

chapters.title: आरोह: उमाशंकर जोशी — छोटा मेरा खेत; बगुलों के पंख

concepts.text: Umashankar Joshi (1911-1988), born at Bamna (Gujarat); Gujarati poet
Works: विश्व शांति, गंगोत्री, निशीथ (Jnanpith), प्राचीना, आतिथ्य, महाप्रस्थान, अभिज्ञा
The poet's page is a small square field
A storm of feelings sows the seed of an idea
The idea melts and sprouts into words
Leaves and flowers grow: the poem takes shape
Fruit of rasa flows forever; poetry is an endless harvest
Evening sky with black clouds
A line of white herons flies across
Their beauty holds the poet's eyes
He asks someone to stop them: beauty's spell
Poetry as farming: process of creation
Beauty of nature and its hold on the mind
सांगरूपक (extended metaphor): paper as field
Colour contrast: black clouds, white herons
अनुप्रास, बिंब
चौकोना: square; बीज: seed; अंकुर: sprout
रस, अक्षय पात्र: endless vessel; लुनाई: harvest
पाँती: line; माया: spell

Mahadevi Verma (1907-1987), born in Farrukhabad; Chhayavad poet called आधुनिक मीरा
Poetry: नीहार, रश्मि, नीरजा, सांध्यगीत, दीपशिखा, यामा (Jnanpith)
Prose: अतीत के चलचित्र, स्मृति की रेखाएँ, पथ के साथी, श्रृंखला की कड़ियाँ, मेरा परिवार
Bhaktin's real name is Lachhmin (Lakshmi), from Jhusi village near Allahabad
She was married young; her stepmother hid her father's death from her
Her in-laws taunted her for having only daughters
Her husband loved her; they lived separately
Her husband died young; she refused to remarry and ran the farm
Her eldest daughter was widowed; relatives forced the daughter into marriage with an idle man
Panchayat's decision forced the marriage; family fell into poverty
Unable to pay rent (लगान), she was made to stand in the sun
She came to the city to serve Mahadevi; shaved head and kanthi mala gave her the name Bhaktin
She cooks simple village food and makes the author adjust to her ways
She hides money and argues cleverly to justify small lies
She refuses to learn to read and sign
She stays with the author in all situations, ready even to go to jail with her
Loyal, hardworking, self-respecting
Stubborn and clever in argument
Truth-bending when it suits her
Strong woman fighting against patriarchy
Women's suffering in a patriarchal society
Preference for sons; widow's plight
Bond between master and servant
Genre: संस्मरणात्मक रेखाचित्र (memoir sketch)
Humour, irony and sympathy in description
Tatsam words with village dialect
भक्तिन: devotee woman; कंठी माला: bead necklace
लगान: land rent; पंचायत: village council
तीतरबाज़: idle man; अँगूठा: thumbprint

Jainendra Kumar (1905-1988), born at Kauriyaganj, Aligarh; psychological novelist
Novels: परख, सुनीता, त्यागपत्र, कल्याणी; stories: वातायन, एक रात, दो चिड़ियाँ, पाजेब
Essays: प्रस्तुत प्रश्न, जड़ की बात, पूर्वोदय, साहित्य का श्रेय और प्रेय, सोच-विचार
A friend goes to buy a small thing and returns with many parcels: purchasing power at work
Another friend goes with an empty mind and returns empty-handed, unable to choose
Bazaar's magic works when the mind is empty and the purse full
Go to the bazaar knowing what you need
Closing the mind (forced restraint) is not the answer
Bhagat ji sells churan, earns only a little each day and gives the rest away
He buys only cumin and black salt; the bazaar's charm does not touch him
Satirical power of money: a passing car makes a pedestrian feel small
बाज़ारूपन: deceit and exploitation in trade
Those who know their need give the bazaar its true meaning
Consumerism and the pull of the market
Self-restraint and contentment
Need vs desire; market as exploitation
Purchasing power used for social good
Conversational, philosophical essay
Direct address to the reader
Code-mixing (Hindi-English words)
Particles ही, भी, तो (निपात)

उपभोक्तावाद: consumerism; संयम: restraint; संतोष: contentment
निस्पृहता: detachment; पेशगी: advance; हाट: rural market

sections.name: 11.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / आपसदारी / विज्ञापन की दुनिया / भाषा की बात / चर्चा करें

Two types of customers and which you are

chapters.title: आरोह: धर्मवीर भारती — काले मेघा पानी दे

concepts.text: Dharmvir Bharati (1926-1997), born in Allahabad; editor of धर्मयुग
Works: गुनाहों का देवता, सूरज का सातवाँ घोड़ा, अंधा युग, कनुप्रिया, ठंडा लोहा, ठेले पर हिमालय
Padma Shri
In a drought, boys' group इंदर सेना roams village lanes
They shout 'काले मेघा पानी दे' and 'गगरी फूटी बैल पियासा'
Women throw buckets of water on them from rooftops
The author, an Arya Samaji boy, calls it superstition and waste of water
His beloved Jiji makes him join rituals
Jiji explains: give first to receive; sacrifice brings rewards
Example: farmer sows seed (gives) before harvest
Author reflects on India after freedom: we demand without sacrifice
The pot stays broken: our hopes remain unfulfilled
लेखक: rational, questioning boy
जीजी: loving, faithful, wise woman
Faith vs reason (लोक-विश्वास बनाम विज्ञान)
Sacrifice and giving
National character and corruption
Memoir (संस्मरण)
Folk songs and village words
Reflective, critical tone
इंदर सेना / मेंढक मंडली: rain-calling group
अर्घ्य: water offering; त्याग: sacrifice; दान: giving
गगरी: pot; पियासा: thirsty
